cards.text: Jesus has been going back and forth with the Pharisees, and now He turns to His disciples. He tells them, "It is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the one through whom they come!" A woe, friend. Nobody wants a woe with their name on it.

cards.question: Jesus says it would be better for that person to be thrown into the sea with a millstone hung around his neck than to do what?

answers.text: Cause one of these little ones to stumble
Speak against one of the prophets
Break one of the Sabbath laws

cards.text: A millstone around the neck, into the sea, and THAT'S the better option. Then Jesus tells them, "Watch yourselves."

cards.question: Jesus tells His disciples that if your brother sins, you ___ him. And if he repents, you ___ him.

cards.text: Then Jesus takes it further. Say the same brother sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times he comes back saying he repents.

cards.question: Jesus says that once your brother sins against you for the seventh time in one day, you can stop forgiving him.

cards.text: SEVEN times. In ONE day. Friend, I once gave an oven the side-eye over ONE burnt batch.

cards.question: After hearing Jesus talk about forgiving seven times in a day, the apostles say something to the Lord. What do they ask for?

cards.text: The Lord answers with a picture: a mulberry tree, and someone telling it to be uprooted and planted in the sea.

cards.question: In Jesus' picture, how much faith does it take to tell the mulberry tree to be uprooted and planted in the sea and have it obey you?

answers.text: Faith the size of a mustard seed

cards.text: A mustard seed, friend. CRUMB-sized! The apostles ask for a bigger batch of faith, and Jesus says even a crumb's worth gets a tree to obey.

cards.question: Next Jesus pictures a servant coming in from plowing or shepherding in the field. In that picture, the master tells him to sit down and eat right away.
Instead of sitting the servant down to eat, what does the master in Jesus' picture tell him to do first?

answers.text: Prepare his meal and serve him
Wash up and rest a while
Go back out and finish plowing

cards.text: Straight off the field and into serving, and I respect it, because I haven't taken this apron off since the day I got here. Then Jesus asks, "Does he thank the servant because he did what he was told?"

cards.question: Jesus asks if the master thanks the servant because he did what he was told. What answer is His question pointing to?

answers.text: No because he only did what he was told
Yes because he worked so hard for it
Yes because he served the meal well

cards.text: Then Jesus brings the picture home to His disciples: so you also, when you have done everything commanded of you.

cards.question: When the disciples have done everything commanded of them, what does Jesus say they should say?
Jesus tells His disciples that once they've done everything commanded of them, they've gone above and beyond what was asked.

cards.text: "We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty." Friend, I get to bake cookies for the Marriage Supper of the Lamb, and if I EVER ask for a thank-you card, slide me right back into that junk drawer.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: "Jesus has been going back and forth...", "He tells them...", "A woe, friend." and "Nobody wants a woe with their name on it."

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card brings in context from outside the passage (Jesus' exchange with the Pharisees, Luke 16:14-15) with no reference. It also cites only Luke 17:1. "Going back and forth" also stretches the text, which has one sneer from the Pharisees and Jesus' reply and teaching.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card only reacts to verse 4, which card 5 already told and card 6 already asked about. It doesn't move the passage forward. It is a joke card on its own, and at three sentences it is also longer than the 1 to 2 sentence limit.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This story card recaps verse 6 ("The apostles ask for a bigger batch of faith, and Jesus says even a crumb's worth gets a tree to obey"), which cards 9 and 10 already covered. It adds nothing new from the passage and runs three sentences.

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It is the only "No" against two "Yes" answers, and it repeats the question's own wording ("did what he was told"). The answers should differ in content, not just in yes or no.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.
